doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Norvo's band, Eddie Sauter and the arrangements
summary: Norvo had double reeds and good arrangers; Sauter had started as a trumpeter with Red.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But Red had a good band in those days. Eddie Sauter wrote for him and a guy by the name of Johnny Thompson, who was studying with Eddie Sauter. So we had all good arrangements. And he had double reeds, like oboes, bassoons —
So that’s where Eddie Sauter got that thing in his head.

Well he had that, because he had worked with Red. You know he was the trumpet player. And he played third trumpet with Red. He said if that would have been fourth he would have played fourth. But he ended up a writer. And he wrote great. But that’s how he started with Red.
